criteria.name: Introduction: mission concept and rationale - Include the following required information: • What is the spacecraft's primary mission? • Why is the mission needed? • How many spacecraft are used and why? • Who are the users (operator and customers)?
criteria.reasoning: Primary mission (coral reef / ocean monitoring with fluid lensing) clearly stated, rationale with bleaching stats and Australia benefit given, single spacecraft justified, operator/customers identified (CSIRO/BOM, Aus Gov/Uni). References included.

evidence.quote: fluid lensing has been used in combination with AI analysis to detect colour/tone changes
Other Earth observation satellites use networks or constellations... Thus, only one satellite is required
likely be used by governmental and science agencies (e.g. CSIRO, BOM)

criteria.name: Main body: mission design - Present a summary of the mission design using software and/or hand calculations as appropriate - Include relevant screenshots and software files (in the main body of the report and/or appendix) - Include the following information: • Where it will launch from, and using which launch vehicle? Why did you choose this option? • What type of orbit will you use? What are its characteristics and orbital elements? • Will you need to perform any orbital maneuvers? • Which ground control facilities will you use? • How often will your spacecraft be able to communicate with ground control? • How long will the mission last, and what are your plans for EOL?
criteria.reasoning: Launch site/vehicle (Kourou ELV, Vega E) justified with rideshare analysis, SSO LEO orbit defined with a=6971km, e=0, i=97.79°, RAAN, argument of latitude explained, J2 precession noted, maneuvers addressed (direct injection + drag-sail EOL), ground station access report with STK screenshots showing 6-7 passes/day ~580s mean, STK use evident.

evidence.quote: will thus use the Vega E rocket as a launch vehicle – launched from the Guiana Space Centre Spaceport
altitude of 600km requires a mean inclination of 97.7924° for the satellite to remain sun-synchronous
Tasmanian facility is selected – the Mount Pleasant Radio Observatory

criteria.name: Conclusion
criteria.reasoning: Conclusion summarizes launch, orbit, ground station and EOL findings, links back to mission need, notes Vega E risk and alternative Vega C, appropriate to evidence.

evidence.quote: initial problem of not catching coral bleaching events in time can be minimised, if not solved, by the initiation of the ZYZZsat in 2025

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: Logical structure with headings and executive summary, but figure labelling inconsistent, no formal figure numbers/titles, some tables duplicated, Wikipedia used as source despite prohibition, references not properly formatted.

evidence.quote: SATELLITE must provide images for a fluid lensing tool to analyse reefs

technical_issues.issue: RAAN set to 27.33° as initial launch facility location – incorrect, RAAN is inertial longitude, not latitude, and will not start at Kourou longitude. Correct SSO RAAN set by LTAN.
Argument of Latitude used to replace AOP/ν for e=0 is valid, but reported as 0° static; should vary with time - minor interpretation issue.
Vega E first flight claimed 2024 – schedule optimistic, but selection rationale of SSMS rideshare to SSO LEO is appropriate.

overall: Solid preliminary SSO mission for GBR monitoring with good STK support and trade discussion, meeting all space segment sections; presentation and referencing weaknesses and minor orbital mechanics slips prevent higher mark.

feedback.summary: You delivered a solid preliminary SSO mission for GBR monitoring meeting all space segment sections with good STK evidence and trade justification. Strengths are clear mission rationale and complete orbit/ground design. Minor orbital mechanics slips and presentation/referencing weaknesses keep the overall mark in the lower Accomplished/Adequate bands.

criteria.C1: You clearly stated the primary mission – coral reef/ocean monitoring using fluid lensing and AI – with bleaching rationale, justified a single spacecraft vs constellations, and identified CSIRO/BOM and government/university users. Well referenced in Introduction. To reach a higher Accomplished, add deeper literature depth on fluid lensing performance.
criteria.C2: You justified Kourou ELV and Vega E with SSMS rideshare to SSO LEO, defined LEO SSO with a=6971km, e=0, i=97.79° and J2 precession, and provided Mount Pleasant ground station access plots showing 6-7 passes/day ~580s mean and drag-sail EOL. For next level, fix RAAN definition – it is not launch longitude and is set by LTAN for SSO – and ensure Argument of Latitude is described as time-varying.
criteria.C3: Your Conclusion effectively summarises launch, orbit, ground station and EOL findings and links back to solving coral bleaching detection with ZYZZsat, noting Vega E risk and Vega C alternative. To strengthen to high Accomplished, explicitly tie conclusions to your STK results and maneuver evidence from the main body.
criteria.C4: Your report has logical structure and an executive summary and is readable. To move to Accomplished, add consistent figure numbers/titles – e.g. Image 4 – avoid duplicated tables, and replace prohibited Wikipedia sources in your Bibliography with primary sources and apply consistent citation formatting.

next_steps: Correct RAAN concept in Orbit section: explain LTAN-driven RAAN selection for SSO rather than setting RAAN to Kourou longitude 27.33°, and show how LTAN maps to RAAN.
Improve report presentation: add numbered figure captions/titles for all STK screenshots, check for duplicated tables, and ensure every figure is referenced in text.
Fix referencing: remove Wikipedia entries, replace with peer-reviewed or agency sources, and ensure all in-text citations match a consistently formatted bibliography.
